1760: The luggage carousel went around empty eleven times before it agreed to include a suitcase. Patience.
1761: Your suitcase came around the carousel looking like it had a much more exciting trip than you did.
1762: You watched every bag on the belt go by twice, just to be sure none of them were secretly yours.
1763: The carousel beeped, everyone leaned in, and out came a single stroller. Not yours. Keep waiting.
1764: The passport line has been shuffling forward one shoe-length at a time for what feels like a season.
1765: The officer stamped your passport, looked at you, looked at the stamp, and waved you through. Cleared.
1766: Another stamp thumped into your passport, joining a proud collection of places you have technically been to.
1767: The layover was long enough to memorize the ceiling and short enough to panic about the next gate.
1768: A layover is just standing very still in one spot so you can rush somewhere else later. Rest up.
1769: You reached a sign that listed absolutely everything except the one thing you were trying to find.
1770: Every arrow in this terminal agrees on one thing: not here, keep going. So you keep going.
1771: You followed the little airport signs so trustingly you forgot to check if they knew either.
1772: The taxi driver asked where to, and you realized you knew the thief's face better than any address.
1773: Into town at last, watching a whole new place scroll past the window like it's showing off.
1774: The ride into the city took three turns and you already can't retrace a single one of them.
1775: Airport coffee: brave, bitter, and served in a cup built to burn exactly one finger. Sip carefully.
1776: You bought a coffee to wake up and a snack to feel better, and now you're awake and slightly poorer.
1777: You unfolded the map with great confidence, then turned it slowly until the world made sense again.
1778: The map has a helpful dot that says 'you are here.' You are, in fact, here. Progress.
1779: You've been awake so long the map and the ceiling are starting to feel equally informative.
1780: The corridors run so long you started narrating your own walk just to keep yourself company.
1781: You've passed the same reassuring plant three times. Either it's lost too, or you are.
1782: The little shop sells neck pillows, tiny globes, and everything a person forgets they own at home.
1783: You went into the airport shop for water and came out holding a keychain you will never explain.
1784: The gift shop had a wall of postcards for a place you can see perfectly well by looking outside.
1785: Your suitcase weighs exactly one gram under the limit, a packing triumph you know you will never repeat.
1786: One wheel on your suitcase has stopped turning entirely and now simply drags behind you in silent protest.
1787: Your bag came off the belt with a brand-new sticker on it. You don't know where from. It looks happy.
1788: You leaned in every time the flap opened, and every time it was someone else's turn to be happy.
1789: You dragged your suitcase over one small bump and it tipped over, as if deeply and personally wounded.
1790: The moving walkway did half the walking, and you took full credit for all of it. That's teamwork.
1791: You reached the end of the moving floor and took one real step, entirely unprepared for having to.
1792: A whole board of times blinked at once and rearranged itself, apparently just to confuse you.
1793: The board flipped all its letters, changed its mind, and flipped them right back. Very dramatic.
1794: You found the exit sign, followed it faithfully, and it led you straight to another exit sign.
1795: Fresh off a long trip, running on one short nap and the firm belief that you're basically fine.
1796: Your body arrived right on schedule. The rest of you is still catching up somewhere above the clouds.
1797: You're tired in that exact way where standing feels ambitious and sitting feels like surrender.
1798: A clue waits somewhere in this building. Your gate, meanwhile, has quietly relocated. Naturally it has.
1799: The chase is close now. You can feel it, right behind the urge to find a quiet bench and sit.
